143	// authed resolves the request's API key to the member it acts for, or answers 401. Viewers may only read: any other method

145	func (s *Server) authed(h handler) http.HandlerFunc {
146		return func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
147			token, ok := strings.CutPrefix(r.Header.Get("Authorization"), "Bearer ")
148			if !ok {
149				writeError(w, http.StatusUnauthorized, "unauthorized", "send an API key as Authorization: Bearer <token>")
150				return
151			}
152			key, ok := s.store.APIKeyByToken(strings.TrimSpace(token))
153			if !ok || key.RevokedAt != nil {
154				writeError(w, http.StatusUnauthorized, "unauthorized", "unknown or revoked API key")
155				return
156			}
157			m, ok := s.store.Member(key.OrgID, key.UserID)
158			if !ok {
159				writeError(w, http.StatusUnauthorized, "unauthorized", "the key's owner is no longer a member")
160				return
161			}
162			s.store.TouchAPIKey(key.ID, s.clock.Now())
163			p := auth.Principal{OrgID: key.OrgID, UserID: key.UserID, KeyID: key.ID, Role: m.Role}
164			if r.Method != http.MethodGet && !auth.CanWrite(p.Role) {
165				writeError(w, http.StatusForbidden, "forbidden", "viewers can only read")
166				return
167			}
168			h(w, r, p)
169		}
170	}

The main problem is in the store's email check. The import's "email_taken" test depends on `customersByEmail`, which is one global map keyed only by email. Two organizations can hold the same address, and the map keeps only the most recent owner, so the import can miss a duplicate.

Scenario, using the code as written:
1. Acme creates `jane@example.com`. The map holds Acme's customer.
2. Globex creates `jane@example.com`. This is allowed, because `CreateCustomer` checks org ownership (customers.go:22). The map now points to Globex's customer.
3. Acme imports `jane@example.com`. `customerEmailTaken(acme, key)` finds Globex's ID, sees `OrgID != acme`, and returns false (customers.go:97-100). The record is created, so Acme now has two customers with that email. The spec says that case must be `email_taken`.

The import also overwrites the other organization's index entry (customers.go:90), so Globex's customer can no longer be found by email. The existing test only covers the case where Acme has no such customer, so it doesn't catch this.

Fix: in `ImportCustomers`, build the organization's own email set before the loop by iterating `s.customers` for `OrgID == orgID`, and use that set for the `email_taken` check. Add a test where two organizations share an email and the import into one of them expects `email_taken`.
